findings: [minor/reviewer] D1 [verdict; CL10; counterarguments[0]; correctedUserAssumptions[2]] The draft says locking in the price has no value, which is stated too absolutely. That only holds if the price being locked is list price and the incumbent's renewal price stays at or below $14,700/month. The draft admits elsewhere that the 2027-03-01 renewal price is unknown (G3, tradeoff 3, furtherResearch item 2). It also allows that a negotiated Lumen rate may exist (CL6). If the lock covers a discounted rate, or the incumbent raises its price sharply at renewal, a lock could be worth something. 'Little or nothing is lost' (tradeoffs) is the defensible wording. 'Has no value' (verdict, CL10, correctedUserAssumptions) is not.

[minor/reviewer] D2 [C3 assessment; CL9; K15; K17; alternatives[1]] The overlap range of 2 to 4 months (E7, K14-K17, CL9, C3) is taken from the packet without checking the dates. Today is 2026-11-11. If quarter end means 2026-12-31, signing then and starting to pay Lumen would give about 2 months of overlap before 2027-03-01. The draft also assumes without saying so that Lumen billing starts at signing rather than at go-live, and that the quarter is a calendar quarter.
